new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (98 pp., Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10171486, text present). The quoted passage is at Supplementary Material 1, Text 2 'Morphophonological processes in Kwadi', printed pp. 10-11 = pp. 11-12, exactly as reported: "As already observed by Westphal, stem-la(a)-stem constructions fall into three distinct tone classes which are possibly linked to the underlying tone of the verb stem (ex. 11):" followed by "(11) Tone classes in stem-la(a)-stem constructions / Class 1 H-H(H)-L k'a.laa.k'a 'fry' / Class 2 H-(H)L-L k'a.laa.k'a 'drink' / Class 3 H-(H)L-L ts'a.laa.ts'a 'go away'" (tone diacritics as in the report; only page-break/line-break differences). The SM2 lexicon pair p. 73 (p. 73) ʔáú-dì 'dog…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kwadi is treated as a register-tone language: every lexical entry in the authors' 736-item lexicon carries H/L tone marks (e.g. ʔáú-dì 'dog' vs ʔáù-dì 'fish', p. 73), and reduplicated verb constructions fall into three lexical tone classes tied to the underlying tone of the verb stem. No word-stress rule is stated and the words stress/accent do not occur in the 98-page supplement.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone analysis is explicitly tentative ('possibly linked'); data are archival recordings of one or two speakers plus 2014 rememberers, and the authors note Westphal's transcriptions were inconsistent. Wikipedia (citing Fehn's 2020 handout) adds that 'the tone system is unclear.. at least two tones (high and low)'.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical/word-level tone on nouns and on verb stems in stem-la(a)-stem constructions; citation forms and short recorded phrases. Nothing on phrase-level prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the same variety (Kwadi/Kwepe/Kuroka of the lower Curoca River, kwad1244); Zorotua/Vasorontu is listed by Wikipedia as a possible dialect but no source examined distinguishes it. Data are archival (Almeida 1955, Westphal 1956-65, Gibson 1972) plus two rememberers recorded by Fehn & Rocha in 2014.
